Historical and Geographic Perspective
The ﬁrst herd animals, sheep, are reported to have been domesticated approximately 10 000 BC. Herd animals were primarily used
for meat and perhaps certain other purposes. The historical record suggests that herd animals during this period were not milked.
Evidence that humans milked domesticated animals dates to approximately 4000 to 3000 BC, in northern Africa and southwest
Asia. Following that time, dairying spread across Eurasia and into sub-Saharan Africa. Dairying was not, however, adopted by all
groups in Asia and Africa who had suitable herd animals. Even as late as AD 1500, the beginning of the great European overseas
